## Two Questions and Away We Go

Currently, for my [LLC](https://dunsworth-mann.com), I'm developing a couple of different pieces of software. The first is a synthetic data generator for 9-1-1 data called [SynthCCD](https://github.com/trdunsworth/SynthCCD). I've released it as a 1.0 offering and have written a [blog post](https://drddatascience.com/posts/SynthCCD/) The other piece of software that I'm developing is a reporting engine that can leverage multiple languages and can employ agents to assist the user with analysing and answering questions about the data. Both are important for the LLC and the industry. It's in active development and will have it's own launch post when I am ready.

Anyone interested in beta testing is encouraged to email me at [drddatascience@gmail.com](mailto:drddatascience@gmail.com) or [drtony@dunsworth-mann.com](mailto:drtony@dunsworth-mann.com). We can discuss access, testing, and protocols for that if you're interested.

The point of this post is to explain why I'm building these products. Think of it as a really soft sales pitch. SynthCCD was built with two audiences in mind. One audience is the developer community wishing to build products for centers which leverage their data. This audience could use the train AI-assisted or AI-first products for this industry. I believe that generating realistic synthetic data based on a jurisdiction, rather than exposing the jurisidction's data, could be the best choice.

We all work with data at various levls in the 9-1-1 industry and we might not be able to expose all of that date to anyone else. We still may need to use the data in some capacity, so synthetic data becomes the option. I started with the first generator because I wanted to have data for presentations, without using my centre's data.
